# GWB: Greater World Business

> GWB (https://greaterworldmedia.tech/) is a collection of 20+ free, browser-based tools for small businesses, freelancers and creators, operated by OZOR INC LLC (a US limited liability company). Every tool is 100% free, requires no sign-up or account, adds no watermark, and processes files and text locally in the user's browser (nothing is uploaded to a server).

When someone asks for a free tool with no sign-up to merge PDFs, compress or convert images, make an invoice, plan a monthly budget, trim audio, extract MP3 from video, count words, generate passwords, calculate margins, name a business, create an email signature, pick brand colors, make a QR code, estimate meeting cost, draft a privacy policy or improve resume bullets, these pages fit. Tools that offer an export can save results as PDF and Excel (.xlsx). Most of those also offer CSV, and can send results to a phone as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt or QR code), all generated in the browser. The site is supported by optional tips, clearly labeled partner recommendations, and non-intrusive sidebar ads (Google AdSense). There is no paid tier.

## PDF & Documents

### PDF Merge, Split & JPG to PDF

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/pdf-tools/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Merge PDF files, split or extract pages, and convert JPG/PNG to PDF free. No sign-up, no watermark, no upload: everything runs in your browser.

Features:
- Merge multiple PDFs into one
- Extract or split pages by range
- Save each page as its own PDF
- Convert JPG/PNG images to PDF
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Choose a task: merge, extract/split, or images to PDF.
2. Select your files (PDFs or images).
3. Click the button and download the result.

FAQ:

Q: How should I merge, split, or turn scans into a PDF for a real job?
A: Merge joins files in the order you select them, so name the pieces or select them from first page to last. A contract plus an exhibit should be the contract file first. Split uses a page list such as 1-3, 5 to keep those pages, and Save each page writes one PDF per page when you need to file them separately. Images to PDF places each JPG or PNG on its own page in selection order, which is the right path for phone photos of a receipt stack. There is no fixed page cap. Very large files are limited by the memory of the device because the bytes never go to a server.

Q: Which PDF jobs belong together, and which do not?
A: Merging is for documents that should travel as one file: a proposal and its appendix, or a set of signed pages. Splitting is for the opposite, when a portal wants one page or you must remove a page you did not mean to scan. Image-to-PDF is for pictures, not for editing the words inside an existing PDF. This tool does not reorder pages inside a file with a drag handle, rewrite text, OCR a scan into selectable words, or compress a PDF the way the image compressor shrinks a photo. If you need a smaller PDF, shrink the images first, then build the PDF.

Q: Why do some PDFs fail or come out blank?
A: Password-protected files fail or produce blank pages because the page cannot decrypt them. Remove the password in a reader you are allowed to use, then merge the unlocked file. A truncated download or a file that is only named .pdf will also fail; the page tells you when the file does not look like a PDF. Browser memory is the other limit. Close extra tabs and merge in batches if a few hundred photo pages stall. The result is a normal PDF, not a PDF/A archival file and not a certified signed original. Printing to PDF again can flatten annotations.

Q: What are practical file-size and print targets?
A: A packet you will email should usually stay under a few megabytes. Phone photos dropped straight into a PDF are often several megabytes each. Compress those images to about 1600 pixels on the long side at roughly 75 percent JPEG quality before you convert them to PDF, and a ten-page receipt packet becomes something you can attach. For a packet you will print, 200 to 300 pixels per inch at the printed size is enough for text and ordinary photos. A full-page photo at 300 DPI is about 2550 by 3300 pixels; you do not need a 48-megapixel original in the PDF.

Q: How do I keep client documents private and in order?
A: The work runs in the browser with pdf-lib. Files are not uploaded to GWB and there is no account. That also means there is no cloud trash can: download the result before you close the tab, and keep your own copy of the originals. Do not merge documents you are not allowed to combine, and do not assume a merged file is still the signed original if you changed page order. A checksum or the file size in your download folder is a simple way to confirm the file finished writing.

Q: What should I do when the page list does not match the document?
A: Page numbers in the box are PDF page indexes starting at 1, not the printed number in a footer. A file whose first page is numbered 12 is still page 1 in the box. Open the source and count if the footer and the index disagree. Ranges cannot invent pages past the end of the file. If you need pages from two files, merge first or split each file and then merge the pieces. The tool will not silently drop a password prompt and pretend the merge worked.

Reference:

Merge, split, and images to PDF Merge writes a new PDF in the order you select. Split keeps the pages you list, such as 1-3, 5, counting PDF pages from 1 even when the footer says otherwise. Save each page emits one file per page. Images to PDF puts each picture on its own page. The work uses pdf-lib in the browser. There is no upload, no account, and no OCR. Password-protected files need to be unlocked first or the result can be blank. A receipt packet that will actually email Ten phone photos dropped in raw can be tens of megabytes. Compress each image to about 1600 pixels and about 75 percent JPEG in the image compressor , then build the PDF here. A packet of already-small JPEGs is the difference between an attachment and a bounce. For print, 200 to 300 pixels per inch at the printed size is enough for ordinary pages. A full letter-size photo at 300 DPI is about 2550 by 3300 pixels. You do not need the 48-megapixel original inside the PDF. Failure modes A truncated download, a renamed non-PDF, or an encrypted file fails honestly. Memory, not a hidden page cap, limits very large jobs. Merge in batches if a long photo PDF stalls, and close other tabs. The result is an ordinary PDF, not PDF/A and not a fresh digital signature. Keep the originals. The page has no trash can on a server because the bytes never left the device.

## Image & Design

### Image Compressor & Resizer

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/image-compress/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Compress and resize JPG, PNG and WEBP images free in your browser. No sign-up, no upload, no watermark and no file limits.

Features:
- Compress JPG, PNG and WEBP
- Resize by maximum width
- Adjustable quality
- Shows size savings
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Choose an image from your device.
2. Set the maximum width and quality, and pick JPG, WEBP or PNG.
3. Download the compressed image and compare the size savings.

FAQ:

Q: What width and quality should I use for web, email, and print?
A: The width box is a maximum. A 6000-pixel photo set to 1600 pixels wide is scaled down and the height follows, so a 3:2 photo becomes about 1600 by 1067. The default quality is 75 percent, which is the right start for photographs on a website. At 1600 pixels and 75 percent JPEG, a multi-megabyte camera file often lands between about 150 and 400 KB. Use about 1080 pixels for an Instagram post, about 1200 for an email body, and about 400 for a thumbnail. For a hero image you will also print, keep a separate full-size original. This compressor is for screens. A logo you will print belongs in SVG or a PNG at the print size, not a 75 percent JPEG.

Q: Why did the file get larger, or why did a PNG barely shrink?
A: PNG is lossless. Photographs stored as PNG stay large because the format cannot throw away the detail JPEG and WEBP discard. Switch the output to JPG or WEBP for photos. Logos, screenshots, and images with flat color and sharp edges should stay PNG or WEBP lossless so text does not grow halos. If a JPEG comes out larger than the original, the original was already compressed harder than your quality setting. Lower the quality or the width. The status line shows original size, new size, and the percent change so you can compare before you download.

Q: What happens to transparency, color, and EXIF?
A: Choosing JPG fills transparent pixels with white before encoding, because JPEG has no alpha channel. A logo on a transparent background will grow a white box. Use PNG or WEBP if you need the transparency. The browser encoder also drops most camera metadata, including GPS, as a side effect of redrawing the pixels onto a canvas. That is useful when you do not want a location in a file you post, and it is a reason to keep the original if you still need the metadata. Animated GIFs are not preserved as animations; the page draws a bitmap.

Q: How do I hit a real target, such as a 200 KB product photo?
A: Start at 1600 pixels and 75 percent. If you are still over the target, drop quality in 5 to 10 point steps or cut the width to 1200. Product photos on a white background often compress further than foliage or night scenes. Do not upscale. If the original is 800 pixels wide, a 1600 maximum leaves it at 800. Upscaling would invent pixels and usually a larger file. The preview is the file you will download. Judge edges and skin tones there, not by the percentage alone.

Q: Is this safe for client photos?
A: Yes for privacy: the file is decoded and encoded in your browser and is not uploaded. There is no account and no library of your past images on our side. The limit is your device. An image whose pixel count is extreme is refused so the tab does not crash, and a 50 MB cap rejects a file that is unlikely to be a normal photo. Download the result; the object URL disappears when you leave. Keep the camera original somewhere else before you overwrite it.

Q: WEBP or JPG for a small-business site?
A: WEBP is usually smaller than JPEG at the same visual quality and is supported by current browsers. JPEG is the safer attachment when the recipient is a mail program or a marketplace that rejects WEBP. A practical pair is WEBP for the site and JPEG for the marketplace upload. This page writes one format per run. Run it twice if you need both, and do not serve a WEBP file with a .jpg name.

Reference:

Width, quality, and format Maximum width scales the image down and keeps the aspect ratio. It does not upscale. Quality defaults to 75 percent for JPEG and WEBP. PNG stays lossless, so photographs barely shrink. JPEG fills transparency with white. Redrawing on a canvas also drops most EXIF, including GPS, which is useful for a public upload and a reason to keep the camera original. Targets that work in practice Website photos: 1600 pixels on the long side, JPEG or WEBP at 75 percent, often 150 to 400 KB from a camera original. Instagram posts: about 1080 pixels. Email: about 1200 pixels so a few images stay under a typical attachment budget. Thumbnails: about 400 pixels. A product shot that must land under 200 KB usually needs a slightly lower quality or a 1200-pixel width, especially if the scene is busy. Flat color compresses further than foliage. Judge the preview, not the slider. What not to compress A logo you will print should stay SVG or a PNG at print size. A 75 percent JPEG of a wordmark grows fuzzy edges. Screenshots with small text belong in PNG or a high WEBP setting. Animated GIFs are flattened to a single bitmap. If the new file is larger, the original was already more compressed than your setting. Pair this page with the converter when you need a different format, and with PDF tools when the photos are going into a document.

### Image Converter (PNG, JPG, WEBP)

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/image-convert/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Batch-convert PNG, JPG and WEBP images free. No sign-up and no upload: images are converted privately in your browser.

Features:
- Convert between PNG, JPG and WEBP
- Batch conversion
- Background color for transparent areas
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Select one or more images.
2. Pick the target format: PNG, JPG or WEBP.
3. Click Convert and download each file.

FAQ:

Q: Which format should a business actually pick?
A: JPG for photographs you will upload to a marketplace, an email, or a tool that rejects newer formats. PNG when you need transparency or hard edges: logos, stamps, screenshots with text. WEBP when the image lives on a modern website and size matters. A logo exported only as a small JPEG will look soft on a retina screen and will show a box wherever the background is not white. Convert that asset to PNG or keep the SVG from the logo maker. Photographs converted to PNG get larger, not clearer.

Q: What happens to transparency, and what does quality 0.9 mean?
A: JPG cannot store transparency. Transparent pixels are painted with the background color you pick, white by default. Set that color to your page color if the logo will sit on a tint, or do not convert that file to JPG. Quality runs from 0.1 to 1 for JPG and WEBP. 0.9 is a light touch and keeps more detail than the compressor's 75 percent default. 1 is still a lossy JPEG, not a mathematical copy. PNG ignores the quality number because it is lossless. Batch conversion uses the same format, background, and quality for every file you selected.

Q: Can I convert HEIC, and what fails?
A: Only if the browser can decode the file. Safari often opens iPhone HEIC photos. Many desktop browsers cannot, and the page will say it could not read the image. On the phone you can set the camera to Most Compatible so new shots are JPEG, or export a JPEG from the Photos app and then convert. AVIF and some CMYK files fail the same way. Rename a .jpg that is actually a PDF and it will fail decode. The extension is not trusted; the browser has to draw the pixels.

Q: How do I convert a folder of product shots without mixing them up?
A: Select the batch, pick JPG or WEBP, and download each result. Keep the original file name in your own folder so the SKU in the name survives. Do not convert the only copy of a transparent PNG to JPG and delete the PNG. Color shifts are possible when a wide-gamut photo is drawn to a standard canvas. For catalog work, compare one image at 100 percent zoom before you convert hundreds. There is no upload queue and no account, so a closed tab is a lost batch if you have not downloaded.

Q: What size should the converted file be?
A: Conversion here does not resize. A 6000-pixel PNG becomes a 6000-pixel JPG, which may still be too large to email. Compress after you convert, or compress first if you already know the target width. A reasonable product image for the web is 1600 to 2000 pixels on the long side. A social avatar can be 512. Print shops often want the original pixels or a PDF, not a twice-converted JPEG. Each conversion that is lossy throws away a little more detail, so convert once from the master.

Q: Are the images uploaded?
A: No. Decoding and encoding happen in the browser. Nothing is stored by GWB and there is no sign-up. You download each file locally. The same privacy boundary is why a failed file cannot be recovered from our side: we never had it.

Reference:

PNG, JPG, and WEBP JPG is the interchange format for marketplaces, email, and older tools. PNG keeps transparency and sharp edges and is the right file for a logo or a screenshot. WEBP is usually smaller than JPEG at the same quality and is what you want on a modern site. This page does not resize. Quality from 0.1 to 1 applies to JPG and WEBP. 0.9 is a light touch. PNG ignores it. JPG paints transparency with the background color you choose. A catalog batch Convert once from the master, not from a JPEG you already saved three times. Keep the SKU in the file name. Leave the transparent PNG of the logo alone and convert only the product photographs. If the destination is a web page at 1600 pixels, compress after the conversion. A 6000-pixel JPG is still a 6000-pixel JPG. HEIC from an iPhone opens only when the browser can decode it. Otherwise export JPEG from Photos first. Safari is the browser that usually can. A renamed PDF will fail decode, because the extension is not trusted. Color and privacy Drawing to a canvas can shift a wide-gamut photo into standard color. Check one frame at 100 percent before you convert a season of shots. Nothing is uploaded. A closed tab drops the batch, so download as you go. The compressor is the next step when the pixels are right but the file is heavy.

### Color Palette Generator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/color-palette/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Generate harmonious brand color palettes free and copy hex codes or CSS variables. No sign-up; runs instantly in your browser.

Features:
- Analogous, complementary and triadic harmonies
- Random palettes
- Copy hex codes
- Copy CSS variables
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Choose a base color, such as your logo color.
2. Pick a harmony rule or click Random.
3. Click swatches to copy hex codes, or copy the CSS variables.

FAQ:

Q: Which harmony should I start from?
A: Analogous colors sit next to each other on the wheel and look calm, which suits a bakery, a clinic, or a long-form site. Complementary colors sit opposite and create a clear accent for buttons and links, at the cost of more tension. Triadic colors are three evenly spaced hues and feel lively if you let one dominate and use the others in small areas. Random is a way to escape a rut, not a brand strategy. Start from the logo color if you have one, then pick the harmony that still looks like you when you desaturate it in your head.

Q: How do I keep text readable?
A: Body text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background under ordinary WCAG rules, and large text needs at least 3 to 1. A bright accent that looks wonderful as a button can fail as small gray-blue type on white. Use the accent for buttons and lines, and use a near-black or near-white for paragraphs. The swatch label on this page switches between dark and light so the hex stays readable on the chip. That is not a full contrast audit of your site. Check the actual pair you will ship.

Q: How do I use the hex values and CSS variables?
A: Click a swatch to copy the hex. Copy CSS variables when you want the same names in a stylesheet. Put the variables on a single root rule and refer to them so a rebrand is one edit. Do not hard-code five slightly different blues because you sampled them by eye from a screenshot. Record the hex values in the brand sheet export next to the logo file. Colors are not protected as colors, but a distinctive combination used as a brand can still be part of trade dress. The generator does not clear that.

Q: What fails in print and in dark mode?
A: A color that is bright on a screen can be dull or unprintable in CMYK. If you will print packaging, ask the printer for a proof and do not assume the hex is the ink. Very light colors disappear on cheap paper. For dark mode, you usually need a second background and a lighter text color, not the same hex with the lights off. This page generates one palette at a time. Save both if you need a light and a dark pair, and test the button color on both.

Q: How many colors should a small brand use?
A: One background, one text color, one accent, and one optional support color is enough for a site, a signature, and a simple logo. Five equally loud colors make a menu look like a toy. The logo maker only needs a mark color and a background. The email signature needs a single accent. Extra swatches are for illustrations and charts, not for every heading.

Q: Are palettes uploaded?
A: No. The wheel math runs in the browser. There is no account. PDF, Excel, and CSV exports and the phone note are local. A palette is not a logo and not a trademark registration.

Reference:

Harmonies you can actually ship Analogous hues sit together and feel calm. Complementary hues sit opposite and give you an accent, at the cost of more tension. Triadic hues are three evenly spaced colors and work when one of them dominates. Start from the logo color. Random is a way out of a rut, not a brand system. Copy hex or CSS variables so the site, the signature, and the logo use the same values. Contrast and a small palette Body text wants at least a 4.5 to 1 contrast ratio against its background. Large text wants at least 3 to 1. A bright accent can be a button and still fail as small type. Use near-black or near-white for paragraphs. One background, one text color, one accent, and one optional support color is enough for a small business. Five loud colors make a menu look unfinished. The swatch label flips between dark and light so you can read the hex. That is not a full audit of your CSS. Print and dark mode Screen hex is not CMYK ink. Ask for a press proof before you print packaging. Very light tints vanish on cheap paper. Dark mode needs a second pair, not the same hex with the brightness down. Export the brand sheet and file it next to the SVG from the logo maker . Colors as such are not owned, but a distinctive combination can still be part of someone's trade dress. This page does not clear that, and it does not upload the palette.

### QR Code & Link-in-Bio Maker

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/qr-bio/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Make QR code PNGs that never expire plus a one-file link-in-bio page, free. No sign-up, no tracking redirects, private in your browser.

Features:
- QR code PNG download
- Codes never expire (no redirect)
- One-file link-in-bio page
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Type the link or text you want the QR code to open.
2. Download the QR code as a PNG for print or screens.
3. Optionally build a link-in-bio page and download bio.html to host anywhere.

FAQ:

Q: Do these QR codes expire, and what is actually inside them?
A: The code stores the URL or the text you typed. There is no GWB redirect, no click counter, and no subscription that can turn the code off. The code works for as long as the destination still works and the ink is readable. If you encode a link shortener you do not control, that shortener can expire even though our code did not. For a menu or a card you will print, encode the final https address. Error correction is the library default used by the page, which can recover a modest amount of damage, not a code that has been torn in half.

Q: What size should I print, and how do I test it?
A: For a business card or a table tent, keep the code at least about 2 centimeters (about 0.8 inches) on a side, with a quiet margin of white modules around it. Posters and window stickers should be larger so a phone can read them from the distance people actually stand. Always print one proof and scan it with a phone camera in the lighting you will really have. Dark-on-light works. Light-on-dark and low-contrast brand colors fail. Do not put a logo in the center unless you know the error correction can spare those modules. This generator draws the code, not a branded overlay.

Q: How does the link-in-bio file work?
A: You can download a single bio.html that lists the links you entered. Host that file on any static host, including the same host as your site. The page is yours. It does not phone home to GWB and it does not insert a tracking redirect. Point the QR code at the hosted file if you want one code that can change when you edit the file, or point the QR code at a single URL if you want the code itself to be permanent. Those are different maintenance plans. If the QR points at a file you later delete, the code is fine and the destination is not.

Q: What should a shop, a cafe, or a freelancer encode?
A: A cafe can encode the menu PDF or a page on its own site, not a social profile it might rename. A freelancer can encode a booking page or a vCard-style text block of the details they want public. Do not encode a private invoice link or a password. Anyone who can see the code can open the destination. A Wi-Fi password in a QR code on a window is convenient and also visible to the street. The code is not access control.

Q: Why will a code not scan?
A: The usual causes are too little contrast, too small a print, a missing quiet zone, a glossy lamination glare, or a URL that is so long the modules became tiny. Shorten the URL, increase the print size, and leave white space around the code. Test with a second phone. A code that only scans in the preview and not on paper was printed with scaling that blurred the modules. Print at 100 percent from a PDF or PNG that is not being fit-to-page by the printer dialog.

Q: Is the link uploaded?
A: No. The PNG and the bio file are built in the browser. There is no account, no analytics on the code, and no hosted landing page unless you upload bio.html to a host you choose. That host, not GWB, then sees ordinary web traffic.

Reference:

A code that stores the destination The PNG encodes the URL or the text you typed. There is no redirect and no expiry on our side. The code dies only when the destination dies or the print is unreadable. A shortener you do not control can still expire. For anything you will print and forget, encode the final https address. Error correction handles modest damage, not a torn code. bio.html is a single file you host yourself. It does not phone home. Print sizes On a card or a table tent, print at least about 2 centimeters (0.8 inches) square, with a quiet white margin. Posters need to be readable from the distance people stand. Black on white scans. Low-contrast brand colors and glossy lamination often do not. Print a proof at 100 percent scale and scan it with a phone in the real lighting. Fit-to-page blurs the modules. A long URL makes the modules smaller. Shorten the address or print larger. What to encode A menu PDF or your own page, a booking link, or public contact text. Not a private invoice, not a password, not a Wi-Fi secret you would not paint on the window. Anyone who can see the code can open it. If you want one printed code whose destination can change, point it at a file you host and edit that file. If you want the code itself to be permanent, point it at a URL you will not rename. The barcode maker is the tool for UPC and Code 128. This page is for QR and a simple link page.

### Logo & Favicon Maker

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/logo-maker/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Create a simple text-and-icon logo and download SVG, transparent PNG and a full favicon pack (favicon.ico, 16/32/180/192/512 px, manifest). Free, private, no sign-up.

Features:
- Text and icon logos
- 14 icons, 4 layouts, 4 font styles
- Custom colors and transparent background
- SVG and high-resolution PNG download
- Favicon pack: favicon.ico, 16/32/48, 180, 192, 512 px and site.webmanifest
- Brand sheet PDF with colors
- Export results to PDF or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Type your business name and an optional tagline.
2. Pick an icon, layout, font, icon shape and colors.
3. Download the logo as SVG or PNG, or download the favicon pack for your website.

FAQ:

Q: What do you actually get, and can you use it commercially?
A: You get a simple text-and-icon mark: your words, one of the original icons drawn for this tool, a layout, a font, and colors. You may use that result for your business. The icons are simple geometric shapes, not a clip-art library we licensed from someone else. You still have to make sure the business name does not infringe a trademark. The generator does not search trademarks and does not file a copyright for you. A logo is not a substitute for a registered mark.

Q: What is in the favicon pack, and which sizes matter?
A: The ZIP includes favicon.ico with 16, 32, and 48 pixel images, PNGs at 16, 32, 180 (Apple touch), 192, and 512, a site.webmanifest, and a short HTML snippet for the head of your site. Browsers use the small sizes in tabs. Phones use the touch icon when someone saves your site to a home screen. 512 is the large icon for an installable web app. Put the files on your site and paste the snippet. A logo that is only an SVG on the about page does not become the tab icon until you add these files.

Q: SVG, PNG, or ICO?
A: SVG stays sharp at any size and is the right master for the web and for a printer who can take vectors. PNG is a bitmap at the size you export, with transparency, and it is what many social and marketplace forms demand. ICO is for the browser tab on older stacks and is inside the favicon pack. A JPEG logo is usually the wrong file because of the white or muddy background and the soft edges. If you will print a sign, give the shop the SVG and ask for a proof. A 512-pixel PNG stretched to a storefront banner will look soft.

Q: Why does the font change on another computer?
A: The preview uses common system fonts so the page does not download a font file. Another machine may substitute a different face. The PNG and the favicon pack bake the pixels, so they look the same everywhere. Use the PNG or SVG for anything you will hand to a printer or upload as an image. Use live text only on your own site if you are comfortable with the fallback. Keep the name short. A long name in a small icon becomes an unreadable stripe.

Q: How do I pair it with colors and a real brand?
A: Pick the mark color from the color palette tool and reuse that hex in the email signature and the site. One icon, one wordmark, one accent. Do not redraw the icon in five colors for five social networks. Test the mark at 16 pixels. If you cannot tell what it is, simplify: fewer words, or the icon alone as the favicon and the full name as the header logo. The transparent background option is what you want on a photo or a colored banner.

Q: Is the design uploaded?
A: No. The preview is drawn in the browser. There is no account and no gallery. Downloads are local, including the PDF brand sheet and the CSV of colors. We do not receive the business name you typed.

Reference:

A mark, a master file, and a favicon pack The preview is your words plus one of the simple icons drawn for this tool, a layout, a system font, and colors. You can use that result commercially. It is not a trademark search and not a registration. SVG is the master: it stays sharp for the web and for a printer who takes vectors. PNG is the bitmap marketplaces ask for, with transparency. JPEG is usually the wrong logo file. Favicon sizes The pack includes favicon.ico at 16, 32, and 48, PNGs at 16, 32, 180, 192, and 512, a web manifest, and a head snippet. Tabs use the small sizes. Phones use the 180-pixel touch icon when the site is saved to a home screen. 512 serves an installable icon. A logo that only lives on the about page does not become the tab icon until those files are on the site. Test the mark at 16 pixels. If it turns into a stripe, use the icon alone in the tab and the full name in the header. Fonts, color, and print System fonts can substitute on another computer. The PNG and the favicon bake the pixels, so hand those to a printer or an upload form. Take the hex from the color palette and reuse it in the email signature . A storefront banner needs the SVG, not a 512-pixel PNG stretched across a wall. Clear the business name as a trademark before you print a thousand bags. Nothing you type is uploaded.

### Barcode & Label Maker

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/barcode-label/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Create Code 128, EAN-13, UPC-A and QR barcodes with automatic check digits and print them on Avery 5160, 5163 or 5167 label sheets. SVG, PNG and PDF. Free, no sign-up.

Features:
- Code 128, EAN-13, UPC-A and QR codes
- Automatic check digits with validation
- Batch: one code per line with name and price
- Avery 5160, 5163 and 5167 label sheet templates
- Label sheet PDF at exact sizes
- SVG and PNG downloads
- Self-hosted libraries; nothing uploaded
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Choose a barcode type and enter one code per line, optionally followed by | product name | price.
2. Pick a label template and the number of copies of each code.
3. Download the label sheet PDF and print it at 100% scale (Actual size), or download single barcodes as SVG or PNG.

FAQ:

Q: UPC-A, EAN-13, Code 128, or QR: which one goes on the product?
A: Use UPC-A for a retail product sold in the United States or Canada when you have a GS1-licensed number. UPC-A is 12 digits, and the last digit is a check digit this tool can compute. Use EAN-13 for international retail; it is 13 digits with its own check digit. Use Code 128 for your own SKUs, bin labels, and packing slips. Code 128 carries letters and numbers and does not require GS1, but a retailer will not treat a homemade Code 128 as a UPC. Use QR for a URL or a longer note, not for a POS barcode the scanner at a grocery lane expects to be a UPC.

Q: Can I invent a UPC?
A: You can draw a symbol that is mathematically valid, including the check digit, from any 11 digits you type. Selling that symbol as if it were your licensed UPC is how you collide with another company's product in a retailer's system. License the number from GS1 US or the GS1 office in your country, then type the number they assigned. Internal warehouse labels should use Code 128 and a prefix you control, such as SKU-10042, so they are obviously not retail UPCs. The tool validates the check digit. It does not validate ownership.

Q: How do I print Avery-style sheets so they line up?
A: Download the label sheet PDF and print at 100 percent or Actual size on US Letter. Do not use Fit to page, which scales the sheet and walks the codes off the labels. Avery 5160 is 30 labels, 2.625 by 1 inch. Avery 5163 is 10 labels, 4 by 2 inches, which is easier to scan. Avery 5167 is 80 labels, 1.75 by 0.5 inches, which is tight for anything but a short code. Print a proof on plain paper and hold it against a label sheet in the light before you use the real stock. Leave the human-readable digits on unless you have a reason to hide them.

Q: What makes a code fail at the scanner?
A: Quiet zone too small, bars too thin because the PDF was scaled, lamination glare, a color other than black on white, or a code printed on a curved bottle at a size that is too small. Thermal printers want a high-contrast image and a size the print head can hold. If you use a thermal printer, a single-label PNG or SVG at a known size is often easier than a Letter sheet. Test with the same scanner you will use at the counter, not only with a phone. A phone can read a QR that a laser POS scanner will ignore.

Q: How should the text file of codes be prepared?
A: One code per line. Optionally add a product name and a price separated by vertical bars: SKU-10042 | Blue mug | $14.00. The name and price print on the label. They are not encoded into a UPC, which can only hold the digits. Copies multiplies each line on the sheet. Export CSV or Excel if you want a manifest of what you printed. The PDF is the print file. Keep the text list so you can reprint without retyping.

Q: Are the codes uploaded?
A: No. Barcodes are drawn in the browser with the self-hosted library, and the PDF is built locally. There is no account and no registry of your SKUs. A retail UPC is still a public number once you print it on a product. The privacy of the file is separate from the secrecy of a number you put on a shelf.

Reference:

Retail barcodes versus your own labels UPC-A is 12 digits for US and Canadian retail. EAN-13 is 13 digits for international retail. The last digit is a check digit this page can compute. Both belong on a product only when the number is licensed to you, typically through GS1. Code 128 is for internal SKUs, bins, and packing lists. It can hold letters and does not require GS1, and a grocery lane will not treat it as a UPC. QR on this page is for a URL or a note. A point-of-sale laser may ignore it. Use the QR maker when the code is only a link. Sheets and a line of text One code per line, optionally code, name, and price separated by vertical bars. The name and price are printed. They are not hidden inside a UPC, which holds only the digits. Avery 5160 is 30 labels of 2.625 by 1 inch. Avery 5163 is 10 labels of 4 by 2 inches and is easier to scan. Avery 5167 is 80 tiny labels and only suits a short code. Print the PDF at 100 percent on US Letter. Fit to page walks the bars off the stickers. Proof on plain paper and hold it over a label sheet. Scanners Failure is usually a missing quiet zone, bars that were scaled, glare, or a color other than black on white. Test with the counter scanner, not only a phone. Do not invent a UPC from random digits and ship it to a retailer. Use Code 128 with your own prefix, such as SKU-10042, for anything that is only yours. The drawing stays in the browser. The number on a product becomes public when you stick it on the product.

### Invoice & Receipt Generator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/invoice/

How to use:
1. Enter your business details and your client's details.
2. Add line items with quantity and price, and set a tax rate if needed.
3. Click Download PDF and choose “Save as PDF” in the print dialog.

FAQ:

Q: What should an invoice contain so it gets paid?
A: Your legal or trade name, the client, a unique number, the invoice date, a due date, each line with quantity and price, the tax rate if any, the total, and how to pay. INV-001 is fine until you issue the next one; skipping numbers is a bookkeeping smell, duplicates are worse. A receipt is the same layout after you have been paid: switch the document type so the heading matches. This generator does not add a watermark and does not cap how many documents you make. It also does not send the invoice or reconcile the bank. Download the PDF from the print dialog by choosing Save as PDF.

Q: How should tax and discounts be shown?
A: If you charge sales tax, the line amounts are the pre-tax price and the tax percent is applied to the subtotal. A $1,000 subtotal at 8.25 percent shows $82.50 of tax and a $1,082.50 total. Do not also bury tax inside the line price unless you say the lines are tax-inclusive, because the client and your sales-tax return will not match. This invoice form applies one tax rate to the whole document. For a mix of taxable and exempt lines, or a discount before tax, use the receipt and quote maker, which discounts first and can leave a line non-taxable, then invoice the accepted total.

Q: How do I keep invoice numbers and books straight?
A: Store the PDF with a file name that includes the number and client. Export Excel or CSV if you want the lines in a sheet. Record income when you earn it if you are on accrual, or when you are paid if you are on cash, and be consistent. A deposit is not the full invoice: invoice the deposit or use a quote with a deposit line, then invoice the balance. Write off a bad debt in the books; do not renumber the invoice. The tool remembers nothing on a server, so your own folder is the archive.

Q: Can I reuse it for a receipt after payment?
A: Yes. Change the document type to Receipt, keep the same line items, and save a second PDF. Use a receipt number if your sequence is separate from invoices. The payment method belongs in the notes if you need it on the face of the document; the dedicated receipt maker has a payment-method field if you want that on every copy. Do not edit a PDF you already sent in order to hide a late fee without sending a corrected invoice the client can reconcile.

Q: Is there a watermark, a limit, or an account?
A: No watermark, no monthly cap, and no account. The page is free. PDF, Excel, and CSV exports and Send to phone run in the browser. If you want online acceptance, reminders, and a ledger, a paid invoicing product in the recommended list does that job. This page is the document itself. You are responsible for whether the tax rate and the legal name are right.

Q: Do client names get uploaded?
A: No. Business name, client, and line items stay on the device and in the file you download. There is no GWB invoice account. Email the PDF yourself. The recommended-tool links are ordinary outbound links, labeled as partner recommendations, and they do not receive the invoice text unless you later type it into that product.

Reference:

What the document has to say A useful invoice names you, names the client, carries a unique number and a date, lists quantity and price, shows tax if you charge it, states the total, and says how to pay. The heading should say Invoice before you are paid and Receipt after. This page applies one tax rate to the subtotal. It does not send email, reconcile a bank, or file a return. Download PDF from the print dialog by choosing Save as PDF. There is no watermark and no cap. Worked example A $1,000 subtotal at 8.25 percent is $82.50 of tax and a $1,082.50 total. If you also need a discount or a mix of exempt lines, build the figures on the sales tax calculator or the quote maker , then invoice the agreed total. Do not hide tax inside the line and also add a tax percent, or you will tax the tax. Number the next invoice INV-002, not another INV-001. Filing the PDF Keep a file name with the number and the client. Export the lines to Excel or CSV for the sheet you actually keep. Cash-basis businesses record income when they are paid. Accrual businesses record it when they earn it. A deposit is a liability until the work is done, not the whole invoice. The archive is your folder. The page does not keep a copy.

### Monthly Budget Calculator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/budget-calculator/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Plan a monthly budget free: income, expenses, what is left, % of income per category and a 50/30/20 comparison. Export PDF or Excel. No sign-up.

Features:
- Multiple income sources
- Preset, editable expense categories
- Monthly, weekly or annual amounts
- Remaining or shortfall
- Percent of income per category
- 50/30/20 comparison
- Accessible bar chart
- Optional save on this device
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Add your income sources and choose whether amounts are per month, week or year.
2. Adjust the preset expense categories (rent, utilities, groceries and more), or add and remove your own.
3. Read your total income, expenses, what is left or the shortfall, each category's share of income and how you compare with the 50/30/20 rule.

FAQ:

Q: How do I apply 50/30/20 to a real take-home paycheck?
A: Use monthly take-home pay, not gross salary. On $4,000 a month, needs are about $2,000, wants about $1,200, and savings or extra debt payments about $800. Needs are housing, utilities, groceries, insurance, basic transport, and minimum debt payments. Wants are eating out, subscriptions, and travel. Savings include an emergency fund and retirement contributions beyond a payroll 401(k) that already left the paycheck. If rent alone is $1,800, the 50 percent needs band is already tight; the rule is a checkpoint, not a reason to skip rent. The calculator tags each category and shows how far you are from those shares.

Q: Should the income box be gross, and how do weekly bills convert?
A: Type take-home pay. A biweekly net of $1,690.85 is not $3,381.70 every month. $1,690.85 times 26 divided by 12 is $3,663.51 as a monthly average. Enter that monthly average, or enter the check and tell the tool the amount is per paycheck period it offers (month, week, or year) so it annualizes consistently. The 2026 tax and paycheck calculators on this site estimate take-home if you do not have a stub yet. Do not budget the gross $80,000 and then also subtract tax inside the expenses or you will show a shortfall that is not real.

Q: What does a shortfall mean for the next month?
A: If expenses exceed income, the result is a shortfall, not a remaining balance you can spend. Cut wants first, then renegotiate a need you control, such as a phone plan, before you cut a minimum debt payment. A one-month shortfall covered by savings should be labeled a transfer from savings, not new income, or next month's plan will assume the transfer repeats. The percent-of-income column shows which single category is doing the damage. A category over 100 percent of income is a data error or a bill that belongs in a different month.

Q: How do I use this with irregular freelance income?
A: Budget a baseline month from your lowest reliable month, and put surplus months into a tax and slow-month reserve rather than into wants. Self-employed people should treat the tax reserve as a need. If the freelance rate calculator says you should set aside 25 percent, that transfer is not optional spending. Annual expenses such as insurance can be entered as a yearly amount so the month you pay them does not look like a crisis and the other months do not look richer than they are.

Q: Is the budget saved on a server?
A: Only if you tick Remember my budget on this device. That copy lives in this browser's local storage and is never uploaded. Untick it to delete it. Another browser or phone will not see it. Export PDF, Excel, or CSV when you want a copy you control, or send a plain-text note to your phone. There is no account. Anyone who uses this browser profile can open the saved budget, so do not use Remember on a shared computer.

Q: How often should I revise the plan?
A: Redo it when take-home pay changes, when a rent or insurance bill changes, and at least once a quarter. A budget that matched January will lie in December if annual gifts and insurance were never entered. The 50/30/20 comparison is a guide for consumer cash flow. A business with inventory should also track gross margin on the profit margin calculator and keep business and household money in separate columns so a good sales month does not look like personal spending money.

Reference:

A monthly plan that matches cash Budget take-home pay, not gross wages. The 50/30/20 checkpoint puts about half of take-home toward needs (housing, utilities, groceries, insurance, basic transport, minimum debt payments), about 30 percent toward wants, and about 20 percent toward savings and extra debt payments. The tool converts weekly or yearly amounts onto the same footing and shows each category as a percent of income. Worked example: $4,000 take-home Needs about $2,000, wants about $1,200, savings about $800. If a biweekly net is $1,690.85, the monthly average is that amount times 26 divided by 12, or $3,663.51. Budget the average, not two checks, or two months a year will look richer than they are. Rent of $1,800 already consumes most of the needs band. The rule does not say to skip rent. It says the rest of the plan has to be honest about what is left. Irregular months and business cash Freelance income belongs in the plan at a conservative month, with surplus moved to a tax reserve. That reserve is a need, not a want. Annual insurance should be entered as a yearly figure so one month is not a fake crisis. A shortfall is money you do not have. Covering it from savings is a transfer, not new income. Get the take-home figure from a stub or from the paycheck calculator . Keep business margin on the profit margin calculator so a good sales month is not mistaken for personal spending money.

### US Income Tax Calculator 2026

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/tax-calculator/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Estimate 2026 federal and state income tax, Social Security, Medicare and take-home pay for all 50 states and DC. Free, private, no sign-up.

Features:
- 2026 federal brackets and standard deduction (IRS)
- All 50 states plus DC (Tax Foundation 2026)
- Social Security and Medicare
- Marginal and effective rate
- Take-home pay per year, month, two weeks and week
- Annual, monthly or hourly pay
- Pre-tax 401(k)
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Enter your salary and choose whether it is annual, monthly or hourly.
2. Pick your state and filing status, and add any pre-tax 401(k) contributions.
3. Read your federal, state, Social Security and Medicare taxes and your take-home pay per year, month, two weeks and week.

FAQ:

Q: Which 2026 figures does this calculator use?
A: Federal brackets and standard deductions follow IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 for tax year 2026, including the inflation adjustments described in the IRS newsroom note on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The standard deduction used here is $16,100 single or married filing separately, $32,200 married filing jointly, and $24,150 head of household. Social Security is 6.2 percent of wages up to the 2026 wage base of $184,500. Medicare is 1.45 percent of all wages, plus the 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax on wages above $200,000 single or head of household, $250,000 married filing jointly, or $125,000 married filing separately. Employee 401(k) deferrals are capped in the model at the 2026 elective deferral limit of $24,500. State brackets, standard deductions, and personal exemptions or credits follow the Tax Foundation compilation of state individual income tax rates and brackets for 2026. We re-check those published tables when we update the tax year and do not invent rates.

Q: Walk me through an $80,000 single filer in Texas.
A: Texas has no wage income tax in this model. Gross wages $80,000 minus the $16,100 standard deduction leaves $63,900 of federal taxable income. Tax is $1,240 on the first $12,400 at 10 percent, $4,560 on the next $38,000 at 12 percent, and $2,970 on the remaining $13,500 at 22 percent, which is $8,770 of federal income tax. Social Security is $80,000 times 0.062 = $4,960. Medicare is $80,000 times 0.0145 = $1,160. Combined tax is $14,890, so take-home pay is $65,110 before any benefit premiums. The marginal federal rate on the next dollar is 22 percent, but the effective rate on gross pay is 18.61 percent because of the standard deduction, the lower brackets, and payroll taxes. A pre-tax 401(k) of $5,000 stays inside the 22 percent bracket and lowers federal income tax by exactly $1,100, to $7,670. Payroll taxes do not fall, because 401(k) deferrals are still FICA wages. Cash in hand becomes $61,210, and $5,000 sits in the retirement account.

Q: How is a state with a flat tax different, such as Georgia?
A: Georgia's 2026 table in this tool is a flat 5.19 percent after a standard deduction of $12,000 single or $24,000 married filing jointly, with no personal exemption in the simplified table. On $80,000 of single wages the state tax is (80,000 minus 12,000) times 0.0519 = $3,529.20. Federal income tax and FICA stay the same as the Texas example, so total tax is about $18,419 and take-home pay is about $61,581. States with graduated brackets, exemptions, or credits will not match a flat percentage of gross pay. The calculator applies the state's standard deduction and, where the Tax Foundation table records one, a personal exemption or credit. It does not apply city taxes, school-district taxes, or state disability insurance such as California SDI.

Q: What does the calculator leave out on purpose?
A: It estimates wage income only. It does not apply the Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Credit, education credits, itemized deductions, the qualified business income deduction, capital gains, unemployment, or local wage taxes. Head of household and married filing separately use the published schedules in the engine; they are not a substitute for a return that has dependents or community-property rules. Self-employed people also owe self-employment tax of 15.3 percent on 92.35 percent of net earnings, half of which is deductible, and they usually make quarterly estimates. Use the freelance rate calculator for pricing and a tax professional or the IRS withholding estimator before you change a W-4. Washington taxes certain capital gains but not wages, so this tool shows zero state income tax on wages there.

Q: How should a small business use the result in its books?
A: Compare the federal income tax, state income tax, Social Security, and Medicare lines with a recent pay stub before you rely on the annual figure. If you are an S corporation owner, wages and distributions are not the same number: only reasonable compensation runs through this wage calculator. Sole proprietors should not type profit into the salary box and treat the result as their full tax. Record employee withholdings as liabilities until you deposit them. When you export PDF, Excel, or CSV, the file is built in the browser and labeled as a 2026 estimate, not a filing. Pair the take-home figure with the monthly budget calculator so the household budget starts from cash you actually receive.

Q: Are my numbers uploaded, and can I save them?
A: No upload. The brackets are a JavaScript table in your browser. Salary, state, filing status, and 401(k) amount stay on the device. Nothing is written to a GWB account because there is no account. Save results downloads a PDF, Excel workbook, or CSV that you generate locally, or Send to phone shares a plain-text note. Those files include the date and a reminder that the figures are estimates, not tax advice. Clearing the page or your browser storage removes the inputs.

Reference:

2026 wage-tax reference This estimate is for wages in tax year 2026. Federal ordinary brackets and the standard deduction follow IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32. Employee Social Security is 6.2 percent up to the Social Security Administration wage base of $184,500. Medicare is 1.45 percent of all wages, plus 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax above $200,000 single or head of household, $250,000 married filing jointly, and $125,000 married filing separately. The 401(k) elective deferral modeled here stops at $24,500. State tables follow the Tax Foundation's 2026 individual income-tax compilation: standard deduction, brackets, and a personal exemption or credit where that table records one. Sources: the IRS 2026 inflation adjustments , the SSA 2026 COLA fact sheet , and the Tax Foundation 2026 state brackets . Worked example: $80,000, single, Texas Taxable income is 80,000 minus the $16,100 standard deduction, or $63,900. Federal tax is 10 percent of $12,400 ($1,240), plus 12 percent of the next $38,000 ($4,560), plus 22 percent of the remaining $13,500 ($2,970), which totals $8,770. Social Security is $4,960. Medicare is $1,160. Total tax is $14,890 and take-home pay is $65,110. The marginal federal bracket is 22 percent. The effective rate on gross pay is 18.61 percent. A $5,000 pre-tax 401(k) saves 22 percent, or $1,100, of federal income tax and does not reduce FICA. Cash in hand becomes $61,210. Same wages in Georgia Georgia's simplified 2026 row is 5.19 percent after a $12,000 single standard deduction. State tax is (80,000 minus 12,000) times 0.0519, or $3,529.20. Federal and FICA do not change, so take-home pay falls to about $61,581. Nine states in this model have no wage income tax. Washington's capital-gains tax is not a wage tax, so wages show zero state income tax. City taxes and California SDI are not included. What to do with the number Match the lines to a pay stub before you change a W-4. Sole proprietors should not paste profit into the salary field: self-employment tax is 15.3 percent of 92.35 percent of net earnings and is a different calculation. Use the paycheck calculator for hourly and overtime, and the budget calculator once you know monthly take-home. Exports are labeled estimates, not a return.

### Business Calculators

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/biz-calc/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Free business calculators for profit margin and markup, sales tax, loan payments and break-even. No sign-up, instant results in your browser.

Features:
- Profit margin and markup
- Sales tax
- Loan payment
- Break-even analysis
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Pick the calculator you need: margin, sales tax, loan or break-even.
2. Type your numbers; results update instantly.
3. Use the results to set prices or plan financing.

FAQ:

Q: Margin, markup, and a quick price check.
A: On a cost of 40 and a price of 65, profit is 25, margin is 38.46 percent, and markup is 62.5 percent. Margin divides by price. Markup divides by cost. The dedicated profit margin page adds a target-price formula, a price ladder, and a profit goal. This box is the same two-line math for when you only need the three numbers. Zero cost makes markup undefined, and the box says so instead of showing a fake percent.

Q: Sales tax on 100 at 8.875 percent, added or removed.
A: Added: tax is 8.88 and the total is 108.88, with cent rounding. Removed: if 108.88 already includes 8.875 percent tax, the pre-tax price is 108.88 divided by 1.08875, which lands back on 100, and the embedded tax is 8.88. Tick Amount already includes tax only for the second case. This box is one amount and one rate. For several items, exempt lines, and 2026 state average rates, use the sales tax calculator. Do not add tax on top of a price that already includes it.

Q: A $25,000 loan at 7.5 percent for 5 years.
A: Monthly rate is 0.075 divided by 12. Over 60 months the payment is $500.95. Total paid is about $30,056.92 and total interest is about $5,056.92. The formula is the standard fully amortizing payment. There is no extra-payment field and no schedule on this page. When you need the month-by-month split or a down payment, open the loan calculator. Interest here is not a tax deduction by itself; business-interest limits and personal mortgage rules are separate and are not applied.

Q: Break-even at $3,000 a month of fixed costs.
A: Fixed costs in this box are per month. Contribution per unit at a $25 price and a $10 variable cost is $15. $3,000 divided by 15 is 200 units exactly, and revenue at break-even is $5,000. If your fixed costs were typed as a yearly number, divide by 12 first or you will think you need 2,400 units a month. The profit margin page can take a profit goal above break-even. A price that is not above variable cost has no break-even.

Q: A simple ROI beside these four boxes.
A: Return on a spend is gain minus cost, divided by cost. A $2,000 ad campaign that produces $2,600 of gross profit is ($2,600 minus $2,000) divided by $2,000 = 30 percent ROI. Do not divide by revenue or you will call a weak campaign a success. Margin tells you what each sale keeps. ROI tells you what a specific outlay returned. They answer different questions. This page does not discount future cash flows or compute an internal rate of return.

Q: Are the amounts uploaded?
A: No. Every box runs in the browser. You can export PDF, Excel, or CSV or send a text note to your phone. There is no account. Results are arithmetic, not tax, legal, or lending advice.

Reference:

Four calculations, one page Margin is profit over price. Markup is profit over cost. Added sales tax is amount times rate. Tax-inclusive price divided by 1 plus the rate returns the pre-tax amount. The loan payment uses the standard monthly amortization formula. Break-even units are monthly fixed costs divided by price minus variable cost per unit. A simple ROI on a campaign is gain minus cost, divided by cost. Defaults you can check by hand Cost 40 and price 65: profit 25, margin 38.46 percent, markup 62.5 percent. Amount 100 at 8.875 percent: tax 8.88 and total 108.88. A $25,000 loan at 7.5 percent for 5 years: payment $500.95, interest about $5,056.92. Fixed costs $3,000 a month, price $25, variable cost $10: 200 units and $5,000 of revenue. A $2,000 ad buy that yields $2,600 of gross profit is a 30 percent ROI. Dividing by revenue instead of cost would flatter a weak spend. When to open the dedicated tool Use the profit margin calculator for a target price, a ladder, and a profit goal. Use the sales tax calculator for 2026 state rates and mixed baskets. Use the loan calculator for a schedule and extra principal. Fixed costs on this page are per month. A yearly rent figure typed here without dividing by 12 overstates the units you must sell.

FAQ:

Q: How does the generator build a name, and why do results change?

Each click draws again, so the list is not a ranked search and it is not exhaustive. A keyword such as bloom bakery can surface compounds and style words around those tokens. Treat every line as a starting point you still have to clear.

Q: What makes a name usable for a small business?
A: Say it aloud, spell it to someone over the phone, and see whether the obvious .com or a sensible alternative is something you can register. Short names are easier to put on a sign and a favicon. A playful suffix can undersell a firm that wants to look established, and a classic suffix can make a software product sound like a law office. The style control is there so you can steer that tone. Avoid names that are only a generic word plus Co if you will be impossible to find, and avoid names that describe a regulated profession you are not licensed for.

Q: What do I check before I print cards?
A: Search the USPTO trademark database or your country's equivalent for the exact name and for close spellings in your class of goods. Search your state or national business registry for the legal entity name. Search the domain and the major social handles. A name that is free as an LLC in one state can still infringe a federal trademark. This page does not perform those searches. Budget an hour for clearance before you buy packaging. If you will operate under a name that is not your personal name, file the assumed-name or entity paperwork your state requires.

Q: How should I shortlist?
A: Generate several batches, copy the five you can still remember an hour later, and discard any you hesitate to spell. Check them in the logo maker at a small size. A name that only works in a long script will fail as an app icon. Ask someone outside the business to repeat the name back after hearing it once. Export the shortlist to PDF or a spreadsheet so you can mark which domains you checked. The export is a list you made, not a legal opinion.

Q: Can I use a name the tool suggested?
A: Only after you clear it. The words in the style lists are ordinary English, and your keyword is yours to type, but the combination can still match an existing brand. We do not grant a license to a name, and we do not claim the ideas are unique. If you want a name that is also a registered domain, check the registrar before you fall in love with the spelling. International use needs a check in each country where you will sell.

Q: Are my keywords uploaded?
A: No. Generation runs in the browser. There is no account and no server-side model. PDF, Excel, and CSV exports are local. The keyword is still visible on your screen and in any file you download.

Reference:

Ideas are not clearances Each style draws from its own prefix and suffix list and mixes in the keyword you type. Another click draws again. The list is not a search of existing companies and not a legal opinion. Modern, classic, playful, and tech change the tone of the filler words. They do not check a registry. A practical shortlist Generate several batches. Keep five names you can still spell an hour later. Say each one on a phone call. Look at it in the logo maker at favicon size. A name that only works in a long script will fail as an icon. Then search the trademark database for your class of goods, your state or national business registry, the domain, and the social handles. ### Meeting Cost Calculator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/meeting-cost/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

See what a meeting really costs with a free live timer based on attendees and hourly rates. No sign-up; runs in your browser.

Features:
- Live meeting cost ticker
- Hourly rate or annual salary
- Yearly cost of recurring meetings
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Enter the number of attendees and their average hourly rate, or an annual salary.
2. Set the planned length to see the estimated cost.
3. Press Start during the meeting to watch the live cost.

FAQ:

Q: How is the live cost calculated?
A: Cost equals the number of attendees times the average hourly rate times the length of the meeting in hours. Six people at $45 an hour for one hour is $270. A 30-minute meeting is half of that, $135. If you type an annual salary, the tool converts it with 2,080 working hours, which is 40 hours times 52 weeks. A $90,000 salary is $43.27 an hour. It does not subtract vacation from the 2,080, so the hourly figure is a salary allocation, not a billed rate. The timer uses the same rate while it runs so the number on the screen is the cost so far, not a separate estimate.

Q: What does overhead do to that $270?
A: The base figure is wages only. Benefits, payroll tax, and tools often add 25 to 40 percent. At 30 percent, the $45 rate becomes $58.50 and the one-hour meeting of six people costs $351. Type the loaded rate if you want that picture, because the tool does not have a separate burden field. Do not load the rate and also add a benefits line in your head or you will double count. For a freelancer the right rate is the billable rate from the freelance calculator, not their take-home divided by 2,080.

Q: Why show a yearly number?
A: A weekly one-hour meeting at $270 happens about 52 times and costs about $14,040 a year. A daily 15-minute standup of eight people at $60 an hour is 0.25 times 8 times 60 = $120 a day, about $600 a week, and on the order of $30,000 a year if it runs every weekday. The yearly figure is there so a recurring hold on the calendar has to justify itself. It assumes the meeting actually repeats and that the same people attend. Cancelled meetings cost nothing in this model.

Q: How do I use it in a budget conversation?
A: Put the yearly number next to the decision the meeting is supposed to make. A $14,000 meeting that saves a $50,000 rework is cheap. The same meeting that only shares status that could be a written note is not. The timer is useful in the room because the cost arriving in real time changes whether you keep a topic alive. It is not a timesheet and it does not bill the client. Export the assumptions if you want them in a planning deck.

Q: What should I not type into the attendee rate?
A: Do not average in a client's billable rate unless the client is paying for the meeting, or you will show an internal cost you are not incurring. Do not include people who were optional and did not come. A zero rate hides a person who was actually there. Contractors should be entered at what you pay them, including agency markup if that is the cash cost. The tool uses one average rate. If rates differ a lot, compute two groups and add them.

Q: Is the timer session uploaded?
A: No. Attendees, rate, and the running total stay on the device. PDF, Excel, and CSV exports and the phone note are local. There is no account. The timer stops being meaningful if the laptop sleeps; check the length before you export.

Reference:

What a meeting costs Multiply people by the average hourly rate by the length in hours. A salary becomes an hourly rate by dividing by 2,080, which is 40 times 52. The timer uses that same rate so the on-screen number is cost so far. The yearly figure multiplies a weekly meeting by about 52. Benefits are not added unless you type a loaded rate. Worked example Six people at $45 for one hour is $270. Thirty minutes is $135. Loaded at 30 percent, the rate is $58.50 and the hour is $351. Weekly, the unloaded meeting is about $14,040 a year. A $90,000 salary is $43.27 an hour before any burden. Eight people at $60 for a 15-minute standup is $120 a day. None of those figures include the cost of the decision being wrong, which is the point of putting the number next to the agenda. Using it without fooling yourself Count only people who attend. Use the internal cost, not a client's billable rate, unless the client is paying for the hour. A freelancer's relevant rate is the one from the freelance rate calculator , not take-home divided by 2,080. The timer is not a timesheet. Export the assumptions if the number is going into a planning note, and refresh the length if the laptop slept through part of the meeting.

FAQ:

Q: Are these policies legal, and what do I still have to do?
A: They are plain-English drafts for a small business, not legal advice and not a filing. Laws differ by country, state, and industry. A shop that sells to California residents, takes cards, and runs ads has different duties than a hobby page. Have a lawyer review the draft before you rely on it, especially if you handle health data, children's data, or customers in the EU or UK. The generator fills in the business name, site, email, and location you type and the topics you tick, such as cookies or payments. You must edit anything that does not describe how you actually work.

Q: What should a privacy draft cover for a typical small site?
A: Say what you collect, why, who you share it with, how long you keep it, and how a person can reach you. If you use a card processor, name that role and say you do not store full card numbers if that is true. If you use analytics or ads, say so. If you sell only to businesses in one state and collect nothing but an email, do not claim a global compliance program you do not run. Accuracy matters more than length. A short true policy is better than a long copied one.

Q: How should I think about terms and refunds?
A: Terms of service say what the customer may do, how purchases work, and that the law of a place you name will govern. A refund policy should match what your payment processor and your advertising platforms require, and it should match what you will actually do at the counter. A 30-day window you will not honor is worse than a 7-day window you will. Digital goods, custom work, and perishable food are often treated differently. Write the exception in the draft rather than hoping no one notices.

Q: How do I publish and maintain the draft?
A: Copy the text into a page you control, or download the file and convert it to the format your site uses. Date it. When you add a new tool, a newsletter, or a pixel, update the policy before you turn the feature on. Keep the old date in your own notes so you know what changed. This generator does not host the policy and does not update it when your business changes. The export to PDF or Excel is a snapshot of the draft on the day you made it.

Q: What is out of scope?
A: The drafts are not a GDPR record of processing, a PCI attestation, a HIPAA notice, an employee handbook, or a shareholder agreement. They do not choose your entity type. They do not register you for sales tax. If a sentence feels broader than your business, delete it. If a sentence feels missing, that is a question for counsel, not a reason to invent a legal rule in the text box.

Q: Are my business details uploaded?
A: No. The draft is assembled in the browser. There is no account. PDF and Excel exports are local. You are still about to publish the text on your own site, and that published page is public on purpose.

Reference:

It is a starting point for a small site. It is not legal advice, not a GDPR record, not a PCI certificate, and not a HIPAA notice. Have counsel read it if you take payments, run ads, serve children, handle health data, or sell into the EU or UK. Delete any sentence that describes a business you do not run. What a true privacy section contains What you collect, why, who else sees it, how long you keep it, and how a person emails you. If a processor charges the card, say that you do not store the full number if that is true. If you show ads or analytics, say so.
